key_insight: Isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me₆) molecules donate one electron to Au(111) and FeCl₂, but two electrons to 2H-NbSe₂.
engineering_relevance: Understanding substrate-dependent charge transfer can guide the design of molecular nanostructures on metallic, magnetic, and superconducting surfaces.
method: Compare isolated Me₆ molecules across three distinct substrates.
Combine scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory with Kelvin probe force microscopy.
Use model Hamiltonian calculations to interpret charge transfer and screening.
evidence_signal: Combined measurements and calculations distinguish single-electron donation on Au(111) and FeCl₂ from two-electron donation on NbSe₂.
watch_item: STS and DFT alone cannot quantify charge transfer in these systems; complementary measurements and modeling are needed.
paper_title: Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
